title: India Women Crush England by 270 Runs to Win First-Ever Women's Test at Lord's
excerpt: Yastika Bhatia becomes the first woman to score a Test century at Lord's as India clinch a landmark victory at the Home of Cricket.
body:
• India won the first-ever women's Test match at Lord's by 270 runs, bowling England out for 186 while defending a target of 457.
  • Yastika Bhatia scored 113 to become the first woman to register a Test century at Lord's, cricket's most storied ground.
  • Fast bowler Kranti Gaud took 5/37 in England's first innings, becoming the first woman to have her name inscribed on Lord's honours boards for a five-wicket haul.
  • The match, played July 10-13, came 142 years after the first men's Test at the venue and marks a watershed for women's cricket globally.

A Victory 142 Years in the Making

The Home of Cricket finally opened its doors to women's Test cricket on July 10, and India ensured the occasion would be remembered for decades. Over four days at Lord's, Harmanpreet Kaur's side dismantled England with a comprehensive 270-run victory — the largest margin in India women's overseas Test history — transforming a historic fixture into a one-sided statement of dominance.

The match concluded on July 13 when off-spinner Sneh Rana bowled Sophie Ecclestone for 50, triggering celebrations that spilled from the field to living rooms across India. England, set an imposing target of 457, were bundled out for 186 in their second innings.

""Every cricketer carries the dream of playing at Lord's."

""Every cricketer carries the dream of playing at Lord's."

Bhatia and Gaud Write Themselves Into Lord's History

Individual milestones studded the match. Wicketkeeper-batter Yastika Bhatia struck a magnificent 113 in India's second innings, reaching her century with a single to cover off her 145th delivery. She became the first woman to score a Test hundred at Lord's, a distinction that places her alongside the greats who have graced cricket's most iconic honour roll.

"Yeh ek aisi jeet hai jo itihaas ke panno mein darj ho gayi hai. Jab bhi Lord's mein 'first team to win women's Test' likha jayega, toh bold aur capital mein wahaan 'INDIA' aayega."

— Sneh Rana, India off-spinner

Fast bowler Kranti Gaud was equally historic. Her five-wicket haul of 5/37 in England's first innings saw her name added to Lord's storied honours boards — the first woman ever to appear there for a Test bowling performance. Gaud's controlled pace dismantled the top order and set the tone for India's dominance throughout the match.

How India Built an Unassailable Lead

India posted 285 in their first innings, with contributions from Smriti Mandhana, Harmanpreet Kaur, and Deepti Sharma steadying the innings after early wobbles. Gaud's five-wicket burst then restricted England to 170, handing India a crucial 115-run first-innings lead.

The visitors tightened their grip in the second innings, declaring at 341/7 with Bhatia's century the centerpiece. Richa Ghosh's unbeaten fifty added late impetus, giving India enough runs to set England a record 457-run target — one that proved far beyond the hosts' reach.

Rana's four wickets in the second innings sealed the deal, supported by Gaud's continued pressure from the other end. Ecclestone's fighting 50 was England's lone resistance in a chase that never gained momentum.

Sachin Tendulkar Hails 'Wonderful Victory'

Sachin Tendulkar, who was present at Lord's to witness the occasion, praised the team on social media. "Every cricketer carries the dream of playing at Lord's. Over the past four days, a new generation lived that dream as women's Test cricket arrived at the Home of Cricket for the very first time," the legendary batter wrote.

"Congratulations to the Indian team on a wonderful victory. Smriti's composure, Yastika's brilliant century and Kranti's five-wicket haul made this occasion even more special," Tendulkar added.

What It Means for Women's Cricket

The victory is expected to amplify momentum for women's cricket in India, coming as the team has already secured its Olympic berth for the LA 2028 Games. The landmark win at Lord's — a venue that carries unmatched symbolic weight in cricket — underscores India's evolution into a formidable force in the longest format and strengthens the case for more women's Test fixtures on the international calendar.
